implementation_notes: C has neither an ORM nor a lock manager, so the cluster lock is hand-built: keep one pthread_mutex_t per aggregate root in a registry that is itself guarded, and hold the root's mutex with pthread_mutex_lock for the whole edit; members never get their own mutex. The database side of the same idea is a root-row lock or, on SQLite, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, which starts a write transaction immediately and makes the database the writer's exclusive resource. Both replace the per-member lock set with one lock identity, and the registry lookup cost is the price of that simplicity.
idiom_name: pthread mutex per aggregate root in a registry (or the database's coarse write lock)
pitfalls: Unlocking a mutex the calling thread does not own is undefined for default mutexes and relocking a normal mutex deadlocks; use PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK while developing and keep lock/unlock in one function.
The registry is shared state: the lookup-or-create step must run under its own lock, and freeing an entry while another thread may still hold it is a use-after-free.
SQLite's BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes the whole database rather than one cluster - correct as a coarse lock for single-node stores, wrong as a per-aggregate mechanism.
